title: Flight Test Other-26a
description: The U.S. Missile Defense Agency (MDA), in cooperation with U.S. Space Force and U.S. Northern Command, conducted a flight test on June 23, 2025, in which the Long Range Discrimination Radar (LRDR) at Clear Space Force Station, Alaska, successfully acquired, tracked and reported missile target data to the Command and Control Battle Management and Communications (C2BMC). This was the radar’s first flight test tracking a live Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) representative target.

transcript.text: The U.S. Missile Defense Agency in cooperation with U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command,
and U.S. Northern Command conducted Flight Test Other 26A, or FTX-26A, which demonstrated
the missile tracking capabilities of the long-range discrimination radar at Clear Space Force Station,
Alaska.
LRDR is a multi-mission multi-face radar designed to provide greater capability to distinguish
and track objects at long range, including all classes of ballistic missiles.
FTX-26A is the radar's first live track of an intercontinental ballistic missile representative
target.
During the test, a target missile developed by the missile defense agency was air-launched
heading east over the northern Pacific Ocean along the Alaskan-Alution Island chain.
LRDR successfully acquired, tracked, and reported target data to the missile defense
system's Command and Control Battle Management and Communications, or C2BMC.
This was the first flight test with a C2BMC tasking of LRDR to track a missile of any type.
In addition to LRDR, the target was tracked by the upgraded Early Warning Radar, or UEWR,
also at Clear Space Force Station, the Sea-based X-band Radar, or SBX, located in the broad
ocean area of the Pacific Ocean and other sensors.
The sensor data was sent to the ground-based mid-course defense fire control to support
a simulated engagement.
Initial indications show that LRDR and C2BMC met requirements.
Program officials will continue to evaluate system performance based upon data obtained
during the test.
The FFX26A will support the operational assessment of LRDR and validation of LRDR modeling and
simulations.
LRDR is the lead sensor in a new class of high-frequency high-resolution discrimination radars that complement
the long-reach capabilities of lower-frequency radars, providing a critical addition to the
missile defense system architecture.
LRDR will provide the advanced sensor coverage needed to protect the U.S. homeland from Pacific
Theater long-range missile threats for decades to come.
